title: Divisible exchanges
summary: A divisible contract separates agreed performances into corresponding parts, so a party’s right to payment for one completed part may be assessed independently of unperformed parts.
notes:
Gill considers whether payment for delivered logs could be separated from duties concerning the remaining timber. The relevant question is whether the agreement pairs portions of performance with corresponding compensation. A price expressed by units is evidence to interpret, not a complete answer by itself.

Distinguish dividing an exchange from merely measuring damages in units. Divisibility affects whether a condition of full performance must occur before any payment becomes due. The parties’ language, purpose, and apportionment of obligations determine whether that treatment fits.
